records.title: Security force near Belgrad attacked after a crossing
records.header_literal: B) UKS v ZON (--- November 7th); 2 TL RICHI-190
records.readable_german: erreicht 9 H. EB?Q. TITEL. Sicherung 219 I. D. noordl. Belgrad durch dort uebergegangene Serben angegriffen.
records.meaning: The surviving second part reports an attack on a security force labelled 219 I D near Belgrad by Serbs who had crossed there. The literal NOORDL suggests north of the city but retains its extra O. The opening fragment, EB?Q field and exact role of TITEL remain limited by the absent preceding part.
notes: The 190-slot native frame contains five source dashes: source 2,21 and 90–92. Four are filled by the proposal; source 91 remains unresolved and gives the internal character of EB?Q with exact domain {4,F,G,U,Y,Z}. No specific name, station or unit is inferred for that field.
DUECH→DURCH, SERVEN→SERBEN and ANZEGRIFFE?→ANGEGRIFFEN require three observed-coordinate substitutions in total. Four source-mask fills separately supply C, E, a separator and the final N.
NOORDL is preserved exactly, including its double O. The preceding part is not supplied from another report, and 219 remains the literal key-derived label.

records.title: Receipt of a FunkSpruch with literal numerical fields
records.header_literal: D) UKS v ZON (--- November --); 1850 1010; RICHI-140
records.readable_german: Fuer O. K. M. Funkspruch EINSA11205BM4 1189 35 vorm. eingetroffen. A. O. K. 11.
records.meaning: The message reports that a FunkSpruch has arrived, addressed for OKM and ending with the proposed AOK11 signature. Its compact reference and time-like numerical fields are retained without reconstructing an exact calendar date or clock time.
notes: The source header leaves the reception day blank and separately prints 1850 1010. Neither that line nor the decoded 1189 35 field is silently converted to a date/time.

The raw O K C M becomes O K M by changing C to the X separator. The raw A O W11 becomes A O K11 by changing W to K. These are two explicit observed-coordinate substitutions; the arrival wording itself is native.

records.title: A prescribed line and a Temesvar headquarters field
records.header_literal: A) UKS v ZÖN (10.55 p.m., November 7th); 2010; 3 TL RICHI-180
records.readable_german: in befohlene Linie NAGYBECSKEREK VERSECZ an, die 10.11 erreicht. A. H. Q. 9.11 TEMESVAR. A. O. K. 11.
records.meaning: This third-part fragment refers to a prescribed line through the transmitted place labels NAGYBECSKEREK and VERSECZ, an internal 10.11 label, and an AHQ field with 9.11 and TEMESVAR. The missing preceding text does not establish a complete movement order or prove that a move occurred.
notes: The native body has 180 coordinates. Earlier OCR attached an extra mask to the five-coordinate VGVGV group, producing 181; it is removed from the OCR comparison rather than excluded from the physical source.

Two ordinary-word/place-spelling proposals change NAYYBECSKEREK to NAGYBECSKEREK and VERSSCZ to VERSECZ. The forms VERSECZ and TEMESVAR remain unexpanded; no modern-place identification is required for the reading.
The printed reception is November 7, while the body retains 9.11 and 10.11. The edition does not rewrite the header to fit those internal labels.
The header visibly places two short marks above the O in the sender label; the transcription preserves this as ZÖN without identifying a different station.

records.title: Danube crossing completed and busy crossing traffic
records.header_literal: B) UKS v ZÖN (9.42 p.m., November 7th); 2010 3 TLE; 1 TL RICHI-160
records.readable_german: An O. K. M. Donauuebergang 21B I. D. beendet. Belgrad SEMUM. Lebhafter Uebersetzverkehr.
records.meaning: The first part reports completion of a Danube crossing and busy crossing traffic at Belgrad and SEMUM. The earlier word layer retains native 21B I D; the separate unit proposal uses the matching p164 passage.
notes: The native body is 160 coordinates. Earlier OCR turned the first-row VDGVV into a six-slot masked group, producing 161; the image restores the actual five-coordinate group without a source insertion or deletion.

DONAUU3BERGANG→DONAUUEBERGANG, BEENDUT→BEENDET, BELGR4D→BELGRAD and UEBSRSETZVERKEHR→UEBERSETZVERKEHR together cost five observed-coordinate substitutions. The raw digits in the damaged words remain visible in the raw layer.
21B and SEMUM remain literal in the earlier word layer. The first and third parts have distinct reception headers; their shared 2010 field does not supply the absent second part.
The header visibly places two short marks above the O in the sender label; the transcription preserves this as ZÖN without identifying a different station.

unit_proposal.readable_german: An O. K. M. Donauuebergang 219 I. D. beendet. Belgrad SEMUM. Lebhafter Uebersetzverkehr.
unit_proposal.assumption: The matching Danube crossing passages preserve the same unit reference, although the messages have different headings and openings.
limits: The observed p153 unit remains 21B in the native and earlier word layers.
The 219 proposal costs one additional observed-coordinate substitution, not a key reassignment or a source transcription correction.
SEMUM remains literal; no missing message part is supplied.

prior_credit: Published period keys: George Lasry, Ingo Niebel, Nils Kopal and Arno Wacker (2016), and George Lasry (2017 key list). Earlier repository OCR and unchanged-key outputs are retained separately. Source review and explicit editorial work: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro. No universal first-decipherment priority is asserted.
limits: All native source slots remain in printed order; no insertion, deletion or reordering.
Unknown square cells remain globally coupled and injective. Roundtrip completion witnesses are explicitly nonhistorical.
Observed-coordinate substitutions and source-mask fills are priced separately. A source-compatible word proposal is not proof of unique historical wording.
